cases.title: An unknown NodeId is logged and skipped while the rest of the polling batch is delivered
cases.intent: A polling Read returns one StatusCode per node. A bad status for one node must cost only that channel: OpcuaSource logs 'Error reading value for channel' with the status and yields the good nodes of the same response. The server answers Bad_NodeIdUnknown on every read, so the outcome does not depend on timing.

assert.text: Error reading value for channel "missing" from source "ua"

cases.title: Server-side absolute deadband (|delta| > 5) versus SFC's ChangeFilter (|delta| >= 5) on the same node
cases.intent: The variable alternates 0, 5, 0, 5 (a Counter with Min 0, Max 5, Step 5), so every change is exactly the configured value 5. The OPC-UA DataChangeFilter built from NodeChangeFilter Absolute 5 reports a change only when |delta| > 5, so after the initial notification the db channel never reports again; SFC's core ChangeFilter Absolute 5 passes |delta| >= 5, so cf carries both values, as does the unfiltered raw channel. All three monitored items are on the same node in the same subscription, so the difference can only come from the two filters, and the boundary is decided by value, not by timing.

assert.comment: the deadband needs |delta| > 5: only the initial notification ever arrives

cases.title: A Percent deadband on a node without EURange is rejected for that item only and never retried
cases.intent: A percent deadband needs an AnalogItemType with an EURange, which opcua-target cannot create, so the server rejects that monitored item while the other item of the same subscription is created. OpcuaSource logs the failed item and drops it for the life of the session; the case proves the rejection is per item: the CurrentTime channel keeps delivering a new value per record and the pct channel never appears.

assert.text: Error creating subscription for source "ua" node "pct"

cases.title: An unreachable OPC-UA server pauses and retries without crashing; ConnectionErrors is not counted (known defect)
cases.intent: With nothing listening on the server port, endpoint discovery fails inside OpcUaClient.create; OpcuaSource logs it, pauses reading for WaitAfterConnectError and tries again, and read() returns an empty success meanwhile, so the source produces no records while another schedule in the same SFC keeps its exact counter sequence. The waits are on observed retries (two pause lines) and heartbeat records. The metric is pinned: only a failing connectAsync counts ConnectionErrors, the discovery failure path records none, so an unreachable server is invisible in the metrics.

assert.text: Error creating client for for source "ua"

knownDefect.summary: a discovery failure (server unreachable) is caught without a metric; only connectAsync failures count ConnectionErrors

cases.title: Boolean, Int16/32/64, Float, Double and String variables read back with exact values and JSON types
cases.intent: Type fidelity of the whole chain: opcua-target parses each InitValue with the configured DataType, the adapter converts each Variant to a native value and every mode serialises it. strictTypes makes 1 and 1.0 different, so an integer that turns into a double anywhere fails, and the Int64 is beyond the Int32 range. Integers above 2^53 (ADP-OPCUA-DTYPES-02) and DateTime InitValues (ADP-OPCUA-DTYPES-03) are pinned defects; arrays are covered by ADP-OPCUA-POLL-INDEXRANGE-01/-02, because IPC drops multi-element arrays.

cases.title: Integers above 2^53 in the configuration are rounded through a double (known defect)
cases.intent: ConfigReader.processConfig parses the whole configuration into a Map with Gson's default number strategy (every number becomes a Double) and serialises it back before any component reads it, so an integer that a double cannot represent is silently rounded. Observed here through an Int64 InitValue of 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1), which opcua-target serves and the adapter reads back as 9007199254740992; 2^53 - 1 survives because it is representable. The root cause is core configuration handling, so every integer above 2^53 anywhere in a configuration is affected.

knownDefect.summary: the configuration is round-tripped through Map<String, Any> with Gson's double number strategy, so integers above 2^53 are rounded (9007199254740993 becomes 9007199254740992)

cases.title: A DateTime InitValue is converted twice and never applied (known defect)
cases.intent: VariableNodeConfiguration.getValue already turns a DateTime InitValue into a Milo DateTime; OpcuaNamespaceBuilder then converts it again with OpcuaDataTypes.asType, which parses value.toString() as an ISO instant. Milo's DateTime.toString() is 'DateTime{date=..., instant=...}', so the parse throws, convert logs 'Error converting value' and the node is initialised with null: the adapter reads nothing for it. A String variable in the same model proves the model was built and is readable.

knownDefect.summary: a DateTime InitValue is parsed into a Milo DateTime and then re-parsed from its toString(), which is not ISO, so the variable is initialised with null

cases.title: opcua-target serves unsigned variables as signed values (known defect)
cases.intent: VariableNodeConfiguration parses a UInt16 InitValue with asShort, UInt32 with asInt and UByte (NodeIds.Byte) with asByte, and OpcuaDataTypes.asType stores UInt16/UInt32/UInt64 values with toShort/toInt/toLong, so values above the signed range wrap and the Variant carries a signed type. The adapter reads them back from the loopback server: 40000, 200 and 3000000000 arrive as -25536, -56 and -1294967296. The base assertion only proves the three variables exist.

knownDefect.summary: unsigned InitValues are parsed and stored as signed (asShort/asInt/asByte, toShort/toInt), so UInt16 40000, UByte 200 and UInt32 3000000000 are served as -25536, -56 and -1294967296

cases.title: BaseEventType events from an asyncua server arrive with their properties
cases.intent: Event channels subscribe to the Server object's EventNotifier with an EventFilter whose select clause lists the BaseEventType properties and whose where clause matches the event type; received events are kept in a per-channel store and returned on the next read. The counterpart is a non-Milo server (asyncua) firing a BaseEventType event every 100 ms with Message e2e-<n> and Severity 500, next to a counter variable in the same subscription. Every event must carry the configured Severity, the BaseEventType id and a message of the generator's form, and no event may be delivered twice.

cases.title: The adapter connects once a server that was down at startup comes up
cases.intent: A server that is not up when SFC starts must not need an SFC restart. The asyncua counterpart is started only after the adapter has logged its first pause, so the first connection attempt has certainly failed; after the pause getClient creates a new client, connects and the polled values flow. Ordering is by observable events (pause line, server readiness, records), never by sleeps.

assert.text: Error creating client for for source "ua"

cases.title: A data model's configured Namespace URI is ignored by opcua-target (known defect)
cases.intent: docs/targets/opcua.md documents a per-model Namespace. DataModelConfigurationMap passes the model's own JSON object to DataModelConfiguration.fromJson, which then looks up jsonObject[key]['Namespace'] - the model inside itself - finds nothing and registers the namespace URI ''. The adapter reads NamespaceArray[2] (the first model namespace) through a one-element IndexRange, which works in every mode, plus the model's variable to prove the model itself was built.

knownDefect.summary: fromJson reads jsonObject[key]['Namespace'] from the already-unwrapped model object, so every data model gets the namespace URI ''

cases.title: pilot: asyncua server -> opcua adapter (polling) -> file
IndexRange slices array nodes; an out-of-range channel fails alone without breaking the batch
cases.intent: IndexRange is passed through to the server in the ReadValueId, so the server slices the NamespaceArray and a configured Int32[3] variable; a range beyond the array (7:8) gets Bad_IndexRangeNoData for that node only and the other nodes of the same Read are delivered. Single-element slices (ns0, arr2) arrive as one-element lists. IPC is excluded here because it drops every multi-element array (pinned in ADP-OPCUA-POLL-INDEXRANGE-02); IndexRange syntax validation (OpcuaNodeChannelConfiguration.kt:117) is dead code, so only the server ever reports a bad range.

assert.comment: the rest of the batch survives the bad range

assert.text: Error reading value for channel "outOfRange" from source "ua"

cases.title: IPC drops every OPC-UA array value with more than one element (known defect)
cases.intent: The IPC split of ADP-OPCUA-POLL-INDEXRANGE-01, same configuration. OpcuaDataTypesConverter turns an OPC-UA array into a Kotlin List whose runtime class is java.util.Arrays$ArrayList for two or more elements; the IPC adapter service converts it with DataTypes.safeAsList, which casts every multi-element Iterable to java.util.ArrayList, so the conversion throws ClassCastException, the service prints '**** Fatal error converting value' and the channel is silently missing from the record. One-element arrays survive because safeAsList copies those. The base assertions prove the batch itself still works; the pin flips between 'arrays missing' and 'arrays delivered'.

assert.comment: the rest of the batch survives the bad range

assert.text: Error reading value for channel "outOfRange" from source "ua"

knownDefect.summary: safeAsList casts any multi-element Iterable to java.util.ArrayList; OPC-UA arrays are Arrays$ArrayList, so in IPC every array value with 2+ elements throws ClassCastException in the adapter service and the channel is dropped

assertCurrent.text: cannot be cast to class java.util.ArrayList

cases.title: Polling reads the exact BuildInfo/ServerStatus values of SFC's own opcua-target
cases.intent: The base of every OPC-UA adapter case: the adapter discovers the endpoint, selects the None/Anonymous endpoint, connects and reads standard Server nodes in Polling mode. The values are constants compiled into OpcuaTargetServer (product name, manufacturer, product URI) or fixed by the address space (ServerState Running = 0, the default model namespace at index 2), so every record must be identical in every mode. Both components run in the case's own SFC (loopback), so all three load paths of the Milo client and server are exercised; the server port is runner-allocated through a never-started deferred service.

assert.comment: Server_ServerStatus_State is an Int32-encoded ServerState; 0 = Running
NamespaceArray[2]: the default data model namespace

cases.title: A ServerStatus ExtensionObject is decoded into a map and narrowed by a JMESPath Selector
cases.intent: Structured values reach SFC as ExtensionObjects that OpcuaDataTypesConverter decodes by reflection into nested maps; a channel Selector then narrows the map. Server_ServerStatus (i=2256) is the one structure every server has, with constant BuildInfo fields. The case asserts the full key set, the constant fields, the ISO format of the time fields, the decoded enum (state arrives as {value, name, ordinal}, not null - the catalog's 'enum becomes null' claim is wrong) and two Selector channels on the same node. IPC is excluded: it drops the null shutdownReason entry (pinned in ADP-XCUT-IPC-NULLMAP-01).

assert.comment: Milo's ServerState enum, decoded by reflection like any other structure field

cases.title: After the server restarts, the subscription is recreated and data resumes from the new server
cases.intent: In Subscription mode a lost server is detected by the connection watchdog (it reads ServerStatus.State every ConnectionWatchdogInterval) or by the subscription status listener; both reset the client, and the next read creates a new client and a new subscription. The counterpart is stopped after 5 records, the case waits until the adapter has noticed, restarts it on the same port and requires 5+ records after the restart. Its Instance node holds a token unique to each server process and is reported once per subscription, so exactly two distinct instances prove the post-restart data came from a fresh subscription on the new server.

cases.title: The auto-created node id ns=2;s=<Schedule>/<Source>/<Channel> is readable by the adapter
cases.intent: Without data models, opcua-target creates a node per channel on the first write, in the default model namespace (ns=2), with the string id built from the schedule name, the source Name and the channel name, each capitalised and joined with '/'. The adapter polls exactly that id (W/Data/Ctr); a different naming scheme would leave the node unknown and the case without records. Polls before the first write return Bad_NodeIdUnknown and are skipped.

assert.comment: every value the adapter read is one the simulator produced in W (both sources are named 'data')

cases.title: Round trip: simulator -> opcua-target data-model variable -> OPC-UA adapter (polling)
cases.intent: The data flow the OPC-UA pair exists for: schedule W writes a counter into a configured data-model variable through a ValueQuery, schedule R polls that variable by its numeric node id ns=2;i=1001. Both sources are named 'data', so the adapter's records and the simulator's records share one path and serialSet can prove that every value read back is a value the simulator produced. At least three distinct values prove the variable keeps updating; polling may repeat a value, so no ordering is asserted.

assert.comment: every value the adapter read is one the simulator produced in W (both sources are named 'data')

cases.title: Round trip in subscription mode delivers each change once, never a duplicate
cases.intent: As ADP-OPCUA-RT-POLL-01 but the adapter subscribes (publishing interval 100 ms) to the data-model variable. A data-change notification fires only when the value changes (DataChangeTrigger StatusValue) and the store is cleared per read, so no value may appear twice; every value must still be one the simulator produced. The variable exists from server start, so its monitored item is created before the first write and never hits the never-retried failed-item path.

assert.comment: every value the adapter read is one the simulator produced in W (both sources are named 'data')

cases.title: An invalid OPC-UA channel Selector is silently ignored instead of rejected (known defect)
cases.intent: OpcuaNodeChannelConfiguration.validate would reject 'buildInfo.[' as an invalid JMESPath selector, but OpcuaConfiguration.validate never validates sources or channels, and the selector getter swallows the compile error and returns null, so applyChannelValueSelector passes the whole unselected ServerStatus map. The gate is 20 records of R and the slow heartbeat schedule H together: today R supplies most of them as soon as it connects, with correct validation H alone reaches 20 after 10 s, so both outcomes are reached by count, not by time. failFast is off because the correct outcome is a component that fails to construct.

knownDefect.summary: OPC-UA sources and channels are never validated, and an uncompilable Selector is dropped silently, so the channel delivers the whole unselected value

assertCurrent.comment: the whole ServerStatus map, the selector was ignored

texts: is not a valid JMESPath selector

assertCorrect.text: is not a valid JMESPath selector

steps.comment: today R delivers (unselected values); with correct validation R never does and H reaches 50 (25 s). Count-based either way, and H's count leaves room for IPC mode, where each schedule's first read is retried after 10 s

cases.title: Subscription mode reports only changes: CurrentTime is new in every record, a static node appears once
cases.intent: In Subscription mode the adapter creates monitored items (queue size 1, publishing interval = the smallest schedule interval of the source) and each read returns, then clears, the values that changed since the previous read (SourceDataValuesStore). Server CurrentTime changes at every sample, so each record carries a new instant; ProductName never changes, so it is reported exactly once, from the initial notification. A polling implementation would put ProductName in every record and would fail the count.

assert.comment: the initial notification only; an unchanged value is never reported again
each read returns only what changed since the previous read

cases.title: The OPC-UA SourceTimestamp written by opcua-target arrives as the adapter's channel timestamp
cases.intent: opcua-target stamps each value with the channel timestamp of the data it came from (the implicit timestamp query next to the ValueQuery), and a polling read reports DataValue.sourceTime as the channel timestamp, so the time a value was produced survives the OPC-UA hop. Proven as a relation between two record sets, which scheduling jitter cannot affect: join.py (a case fixture, run while SFC runs) matches every R record (value, timestamp) to the W record that produced the value, within 1 us because OPC-UA DateTime has 100 ns resolution. IPC is excluded because it drops channel timestamps (pinned in ADP-OPCUA-TS-PROPAGATION-IPC-01).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. All Rights Reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
"""Join check for the OPC-UA timestamp propagation cases (a case fixture, run as a timeline step).

    python join.py <r-dir> <w-dir> <out.jsonl>

Every record of schedule R (the adapter's reads, in <r-dir>) carries sources.data.values.ctr {value,
timestamp}. The value was written into opcua-target by schedule W (records in <w-dir>), and the OPC-UA
SourceTimestamp of that write is W's channel timestamp. OPC-UA DateTime has 100 ns resolution and the JVM
clock may have ns resolution, so a timestamp matches when it is within 1 us. W is re-read for up to 5 s
until it holds every value R saw (the two file targets write concurrently). One JSON line is appended:

    {"name": "join", "rRecords", "matched", "unmatched", "missingInW", "channelEqualsSource", "ok", "examples"}
"""
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path


def ns(iso: str) -> int:
    """ISO-8601 UTC instant with up to 9 fractional digits -> integer nanoseconds since the epoch."""
    import calendar

    date, _, clock = iso.rstrip("Z").partition("T")
    hms, _, frac = clock.partition(".")
    y, mo, d = (int(x) for x in date.split("-"))
    h, mi, s = (int(x) for x in hms.split(":"))
    return calendar.timegm((y, mo, d, h, mi, s)) * 10**9 + int((frac + "000000000")[:9])


def records(directory: Path) -> list:
    out = []
    for p in sorted(directory.rglob("*.json")):
        try:
            data = json.loads(p.read_text())
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
            continue  # being written
        out.extend(data if isinstance(data, list) else [data])
    return out


def main():
    r_dir, w_dir, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3])
    reads = [r for r in records(r_dir) if r.get("schedule") == "R"]
    pairs = [(r["sources"]["data"]["values"]["ctr"], r["sources"]["data"].get("timestamp")) for r in reads]
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
    while True:
        written = {}
        for w in records(w_dir):
            ch = w["sources"]["data"]["values"]["ctr"]
            written.setdefault(ch["value"], []).append(ns(ch["timestamp"]))
        missing = [c["value"] for c, _ in pairs if c["value"] not in written]
        if not missing or time.monotonic() > deadline:
            break
        time.sleep(0.2)
    matched, unmatched, examples, same = 0, 0, [], 0
    for ch, source_ts in pairs:
        if source_ts is not None and ch.get("timestamp") == source_ts:
            same += 1
        t = ns(ch["timestamp"])
        if any(abs(t - w) <= 1000 for w in written.get(ch["value"], [])):
            matched += 1
        else:
            unmatched += 1
            if len(examples) < 3:
                examples.append({"r": ch, "w": written.get(ch["value"])})
    rec = {"name": "join", "rRecords": len(pairs), "matched": matched, "unmatched": unmatched,
           "missingInW": len(missing), "channelEqualsSource": same,
           "ok": len(pairs) >= 5 and unmatched == 0 and not missing, "examples": examples}
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with out.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")


main()

cases.title: IPC mode replaces adapter channel timestamps with the source read time (known defect)
cases.intent: The IPC split of ADP-OPCUA-TS-PROPAGATION-01, same configuration and join. The IPC adapter service converts each single-valued channel with addAnyValue(key, value.value), dropping the ChannelReadValue timestamp, and stamps the source with Instant.now(); sfc-main then fills every channel timestamp from the source timestamp. So in IPC the OPC-UA SourceTimestamp (and any adapter's channel timestamp) is lost: every R channel timestamp equals its source timestamp and none matches the W record that produced the value.

knownDefect.summary: the IPC adapter service converts single channel values without their ChannelReadValue timestamp, so every adapter channel timestamp is replaced by the source read time
